A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RMD research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison, including the additional figure in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original image and video generation evaluations, component and resolution-schedule ablations, and human-preference results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a four-stage resolution experiment in Table 5 and video examples in Figure 13.

M1.justification: The logSNR partitioning, cross-resolution distribution matching, noise re-injection, warm-up, and cascaded inference procedures remain unchanged, including Algorithms 1–2. Clarified notation and testing a four-stage configuration do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use JourneyDB training prompts, HPS v2.1 image evaluation, VBench and T2V-CompBench video evaluation, and the same human-study coverage. The additional resolution configuration and video examples do not establish a new dataset, task, or distinct test scenario.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same comparator rows for each backbone. The new Figure 13 compares RMD with the already evaluated base model, DMD2, and TDM. The added citation beside SD3.5-Turbo does not establish a different evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Table 6 revises shifted timesteps: SDXL/PixArt 857→681, SD3.5 947→865, and Wan2.1 974/937→937/857. Section 4.4 changes the stated default threshold from −5.0 to −2.5, matching Section 4.1. Table 5 adds a 128→256→512→1024 schedule with one step per stage. These are reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 5 extends the resolution-stage analysis from two- and three-stage configurations to four stages, adding evidence about the speed–quality tradeoff under more aggressive resolution scheduling. The component, noise-mixing, and step-allocation ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or variability estimates for the benchmark scores. Existing seed-control statements and the human-study reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: The new four-stage row in Table 5 reports 3.08× speedup relative to its four-step baseline, HPS 29.48, AeS 6.59, and CLIP 33.41. Figure 13 adds qualitative video results. Tables 1–4, existing Table 5 scores, and human-preference results are unchanged. Section 4.1 also newly asserts comparable training cost to TDM and lower cost than DMD2, without the promised supporting comparison.

T1.justification: Equation (6) receives an indexing correction that makes it consistent with the projected distribution already described immediately below it and used in Equations (7)–(8). The denoiser and compensated-logSNR explanations clarify existing mathematics; no substantive new derivation, formal assumption, theorem, or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and fidelity–efficiency claims, including the reported 33.4× SDXL and 25.6× Wan2.1 speedups. The additional evidence does not redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 newly explains that Figure 3 depicts compensated logSNR schedules after Equation (2), interpreting higher low-resolution curves as less effective noise. Section 4.1 replaces 'data-free' with the more precise 'image-free' description while retaining the use of training prompts. No substantive new failure-condition or limitations discussion appears.

D1.justification: The revised timestep schedules and default threshold change the reproducibility information, and v2 explicitly identifies the fake denoiser as predicting clean data. Optimizers, learning rates, batch sizes, hardware, warm-up counts, and noise-mixing settings otherwise remain unchanged. The new training-cost statement supplies neither timings nor the detailed comparison it attributes to Appendix B.

R1.justification: Both versions contain the same 53 referenced works and retain the same related-work positioning. Bibliographic corrections and an additional inline pointer to an already cited work do not introduce new literature or substantively revise the novelty argument.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar, terminology, heading, and explanatory edits; updates author order, affiliations, and footnotes; and adds acknowledgements. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figures 2–3 are redrawn with revised trajectories, curves, colors, and interval annotations; Figure 4 moves earlier. Table 5 incorporates step counts into the resolution column and adds a row. Appendix E gains Figure 13, and running headers are introduced. Other scientific displays are substantially retained.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves the contradictory default threshold, improves notation and schedule explanations, and modestly extends evidence about resolution-stage tradeoffs and video quality. These changes improve clarity and completeness without changing the central method or main scores. The gains are limited by the unsupported new training-cost comparison and the lack of explanation connecting revised timesteps to the retained results.
